title: fix(sdk): keep an uploaded file's name when transcribing
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix `transcribe()` sending every upload as `audio.mp3`; a `File` now keeps its own name
- `openai/gpt-transcribe` (Azure) reads the format from the extension, so WAV files from Play failed with "Audio file might be corrupted or unsupported". The other transcription models sniff the content and were unaffected
- ArrayBuffers and nameless Blobs still go as `audio.mp3`
- Releases SDK 5.1.0-alpha.11 (alpha.10 is already on npm)

Checked: build, typecheck, Biome, 123 SDK tests (new test covers both naming cases). In Play, `openai/gpt-transcribe` now transcribes the same WAV it rejected before; a direct request with the real filename always worked.

gist.headline: A WAV by its name
gist.blurb: The SDK stops introducing every audio upload as audio.mp3. WAV files get to keep their names, which matters to a transcription model that reads the extension.
gist.summary: SDK 5.1.0-alpha.11 makes transcribe() preserve a File's filename so Azure-backed openai/gpt-transcribe can identify WAV uploads by extension; nameless Blobs and ArrayBuffers still use audio.mp3.
gist.impact: WAV files from Play can pass through the SDK to openai/gpt-transcribe without the unsupported-audio error caused by the wrong filename.
gist.visual_concept: Polli hands a clearly labeled WAV file to a friendly CRT monitor robot, whose screen shows a short transcript. The file label is the key visual: the SDK keeps it attached instead of replacing it with audio.mp3. Code-flowers grow around the terminal.
